ratings_why.fun: Real choices every turn: Fruit order as making change, spend now or hoard for Ashcake, and Sexton spending the pile after Ashcake has counted it; Amanita sets off half the tribe at once.
ratings_why.distinct: The reading-order change puzzle is fresh, but a death counter spent by the tribe sits close to the Larder and the Toll, and death-matters is a familiar auto-battler theme.

verdict_why: Two key combo cards, Amanita and Bootlace with Puffwell, need wording a player can read before the design can settle.

points.text: Warden Amanita: 'share its stats' could mean each neighbour gets all of them or they split them. Say which, for example 'split its stats, rounded down'.
Grandmother Bootlace with Bellows Puffwell's 'repeated while you can pay': does each paid fire get a free copy, or only the first? Spell it out on one of the two cards.

Amanita is the best combo hub: one Start of Combat kill feeds Ludwig, Stinkhorn, the Weaver's Spore, the Sexton, the Abbess and Compost together. A second, cheaper self-kill at Tier 2 would let the network build start earlier.
Hired Mute with Old Fingers is a lovely misuse: play Fingers for 4 Compost, then sell Fingers itself for 3 more. A card that rewards selling Created units would add one more off-label route.
Button Mushroom and Pallbearer only fill change gaps. A small Fruit that pays out differently by slot or by what's left over would give the change puzzle a second layer.

standouts.why: A free sacrifice each fight that sets off every death reader and moves stats instead of making them.
Spends the pile mid-fight after Ashcake has already counted it, so the spend and hoard builds meet in one fight.
A flat-rate burial makes worthless Created units and Bellies worth something, with neat cross-tribe uses.

weakest.why: Does one obvious job: pay 2, grow a little.
A plain deathrattle body with no tie to the change puzzle.
A generic 'when a unit dies, buff' payoff; it reads touching but adds no decision.

flags.note: 'Share its stats' doesn't say whether the stats are split or copied.
How the free trigger works with Puffwell's repeat isn't written down.
With the Mourner and Puffwell, or with golden Inkcap at 8 gold a turn, this is the tribe's runaway risk.
Grows the pile by half of itself each turn; on a pure hoard board it can outpace what any Fruit needs.
